title: Onboarding clauses for beta open models with runtime sanity tests
creator: Ethan Morales
description: PRD fragment: define strict-but-flexible intake and acceptance clauses for community-supplied open model weights that are designated 'beta' or 'unstable' at registration time. This ticket focuses on: 1) clarifying what metadata is required at intake (architecture, tokenizer, expected sequence length distributions, quantization recommendations, reproducible inference scripts), 2) defining when and how we apply temporary 'soft pins' vs hard pins, 3) establishing a lightweight automated runtime sanity test suite that runs in the catalog intake pipeline and gates promotion, and 4) documenting required compatibility notes and developer-facing guidance so integrators know expected runtime behaviors and fallback stories.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form includes mandatory fields: model.architecture, tokenizer.id, weights.hash, recommended.quantization_profiles (list), example_inputs (3), expected_seq_len_p95. 2) Registration flow assigns 'beta' tag when submitter selects instability flags or when automatic heuristics detect mismatch with supported ops. 3) Soft-pin policy defined: soft-pinned variants route to a compatibility layer that allows automatic ephemeral fallback to a pinned stable variant; policy documented in 1-page checklist. 4) Runtime sanity suite created and integrated into CI: includes end-to-end generation with 3 sample prompts, KV cache correctness check, streaming-resume smoke test, and a performance baseline (p50 latency within 2x of curated baseline for similar-sized models). 5) Onboarding pipeline emits a compatibility-notes.md artifact with clear guidance for users (known limitations, recommended batch sizes, quantization caveats). 6) Security review completed for models that request access to private infra or custom kernels. 7) Rollout plan for promoting beta models to 'catalog' channel: controlled canary (5% traffic), metric thresholds and rollback criteria defined.
notes: Key tradeoffs discussed: (A) strict intake metadata accelerates runtime compatibility but increases friction for community contributors; decided to allow a 'grace window' where maintainers can request missing fields during staging. (B) Runtime sanity tests must be fast (<10 minutes total) to keep the intake pipeline responsive; heavy profiling deferred to a separate profiling job. (C) Soft-pins help reduce disruption but add routing complexity; tracking instrumentation required to reason about cost/latency delta.
